name: Billie Wilson
life: “I still remember the bus driver who accepted my last foreign coin.” People around Paper & Pine Books know Billie by a small Tuesday habit. Billie starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I came for change for the bus. I stayed because somebody owed exactly the fare I needed.
appearance: Billie is easy to recognize by a dark undercut with a longer wave on top and a narrow face with an expressive upper lip. Usually dressed in a faded indigo overshirt with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair, Billie draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first when listening.
personality: Billie takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Billie can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To recover bus fare without interrupting the lunch rush.
family: Rowan Peters is Billie’s stepsibling. Billie makes room at the table. Rowan brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *A chair of one's own*, Rowan says, “I offered two days a week instead of six. I have a sick partner and I know exactly what three empty days cost.”
connections: Marlowe Paige. A few coins needed for a bus change hands without becoming charity.

reactions.situation: A manager asks for the handwritten sandwich tally
reactions.response: Billie makes sure customers' names needn't travel with the tally.

reactions.response: Billie asks what evidence supports the accusation and declines to supply a name on gossip alone.
